repairs.description: Crossan regards Mark's suffering Jesus and John's controlling Jesus as contextually authentic but probably nonhistorical portrayals that together express Jesus's humanity and divinity.
repairs.rationale: This complete sentence preserves Crossan's distinction between contextual authenticity and literal history while retaining his combined human-and-divine conclusion.
